### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), applyRegistryWriteThrough (symbol, a method of class ProtocolRegistryHydrationFacet))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via publishPackageDrafts (symbol, a method of class ProtocolHistoryAndPublishFacet))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e2eadd2902c3c934c7dcdfaf53206ad41db0b6e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `672a0a4bb0cef66d6553304eb34b4941d7baa754` — the merge of head `2dfe890eee82a22d9850a1125e8c36db2a712b8b` into base `7e2eadd2902c3c934c7dcdfaf53206ad41db0b6e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 672a0a4bb0cef66d6553304eb34b4941d7baa754 && git checkout 672a0a4bb0cef66d6553304eb34b4941d7baa754
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7e2eadd2902c3c934c7dcdfaf53206ad41db0b6e 2dfe890eee82a22d9850a1125e8c36db2a712b8b && git checkout -B drift-repro 7e2eadd2902c3c934c7dcdfaf53206ad41db0b6e && git merge --no-ff 2dfe890eee82a22d9850a1125e8c36db2a712b8b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e2eadd2902c3c934c7dcdfaf53206ad41db0b6e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7e2eadd2902c3c934c7dcdfaf53206ad41db0b6e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head: `2dfe890eee82a22d9850a1125e8c36db2a712b8b` · reviewer review#2 (`session_016WV4cxDxAYxdtDhtR1kQQe`) · area A4 · Fixes #33005

Checked against the maintainer ruling (6879630490, option D):
- **Advisory on the element a client reads.** `applyObjectRegistryMutation` now answers the refusal from its existing `catch`, the one place a `registerObject` refusal was kept to a `warn` line, and `undefined` on every other path. `applyRegistryWriteThrough` passes it on for the `object` branch only. `runPublishSideEffects` turns it into one `RuntimeAuthoringIssue` (`object-registry-refused`, `warning`, `where: object "NAME"`). Then `publishPackageDrafts` appends it to that object's `published[]` element, ahead of the storage notice, and `publishMetaItem` and publish-mode `saveMetaItem` append it to their own `advisories`. The outcome, `success` and the counts are unchanged, and a clean answer adds no key (pinned: the sibling element's keys stay `name`, `type`, `version`).
- **Logged once at `error`.** There is one `reportObjectRegistryRefusal` call per refused object per write, and the test counts exactly one line for each door. The registry's text reaches the caller only through `clientFacingFailureText`, as on `object-storage-sync-refused`. The test pins that the undeclared text stays out of the 2xx body.
- **Stable rule code** for the follow-up card (A) and for cloud: `OBJECT_REGISTRY_REFUSED = 'object-registry-refused'`.
- **`Clause-②: no` accepted. Here is why it differs from #33336:** there, the deciding fact was the new rule id exported from the `@objectstack/lint` root. Here `OBJECT_REGISTRY_REFUSED`, `ObjectRegistryRefusal` and `reportObjectRegistryRefusal` are not re-exported from `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` (the package's only `exports` entry), and the change in the answer is one more element in the existing optional `advisories`. That is the same shape as #30691 and #30754 (`object-storage-sync-refused`), both declared and landed `Clause-②: no`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: what an author can write does not move.

- N1: a refusal now logs two lines, the existing `warn` from the `catch` and the new `error`. The `error` line says the reason is "logged after this line", but it is the second argument of the same line (and was also in the `warn` before it). Saying "(the registry's reason follows)" would be exact.
- N2 (landing note, not a finding): `protocol.ts` is E1's file under the pilot's ownership table. The three signature lines here are mechanical, but check E1's open stack on `protocol.ts`, and #33276/#33193 on `protocol-history-and-publish.ts` as the PR notes, for conflicts before you arm it.
